items.title: '조작기소 특검법' 국무회의서 의결…한 총리 주재
items.snippet: '조작기소 특검법' 공포안이 오늘(17일) 국무회의를 통과했습니다.정부는 이날 한성숙 국무총리 주재로 정부서울청사에서 열린 국무회의에서 조작기소 특겁법을 심의·의결했습니다.이재명 대통령의 아세안(ASEAN·동남아시아국가연합)·아시아태평양경제협력체(APEC) 순방으로 이날 국무회의는 한 총리가 주재했습니다.특검법은 윤석열 정부 당시 검찰·국가정보원·감사원 등 국가기관이 야당이던 민주당과 정치적 반대 세력을 상대로 조작 수사·기소를 벌였다는 의혹을 규명하기 위한 내용을 담고 있습니다.수사 대상에는 이 대통령 관련 사건인 대장동·위례신도시·백현동 개발 관련 배임, 대장동·백현동 개발 관련 공직선거법 위반, 김진성 씨 위증교사..

items.snippet: 청와대는 대학수학능력시험을 앞두고 인공지능(AI)을 악용한 '커닝' 우려가 커지는 것과 관련, 별도의 대응 태스크포스(TF)를 구성하고 대책 마련에 나섰습니다.청와대는 오늘(17일) 임광현 대통령 비서실장을 주축으로 청와대 내에 'AI 악용 부정행위 비상 대응 TF'가 마련됐고, 전날 TF 대책회의가 열렸다고 밝혔습니다.이번 TF 회의에서는 19일로 예정된 수능 시험에서 AI 부정행위를 방지할 수 있는 대책과 함께, AI 커닝 의심 사례 적발 시의 대처 방안 등이 집중적으로 논의된 것으로 알려졌습니다.임 실장은 사회수석실 산하 교육비서관실, 국정상황실, 국가안보실 내 사이버안보 업무 담당자 등 관련 직원들에게 수능일까지..

Surrogate-Assisted Compact-Model Extraction for SKY130 CMOS at 77 K
items.abstract: Cryogenic circuit design requires compact transistor models that reproduce measured low-temperature behavior and run in standard circuit simulators. We fit BSIM4 parameters to measured I-V curves of SkyWater 130 nm (SKY130) transistors at 77 K using a neural surrogate of NGSpice. The surrogate maps compact-model parameters and device geometry to the complete set of output and transfer characteristics. Extraction is a bounded least-squares search: a bank of NGSpice simulations supplies initial candidates, finite differences of the surrogate supply the local Jacobian, and NGSpice re-simulates the resulting cards before selection. On 18 measured geometries, we compare a search over seven card parameters with a search over 43 parameters selected by NGSpice sensitivity. items.title: Energy spectrum of trions in semiconductors
items.abstract: Energy levels of trions in a bulk semiconductor crystal are calculated by two different numerical methods. On the one hand, we construct the finite-element solution of the Schrödinger equation in the total angular momentum representation. On the other hand, we use the Gaussian expansion method (GEM), applied to each of the three Faddeev components of the wave function. The results for the total angular momenta $J=0$ and $J=1$ of the trion were obtained for a wide range of the hole-to-electron mass ratios covering most existing semiconductor compounds. The dependencies of the energies on the mass ratio for trions in a bulk crystal qualitatively agree with the results for a simplified model of a trion in a 1D quantum wire, for which the three-body energies can be calculated with arbitrary precision as well as easily approximated using Born-Oppenheimer potential-energy curves. items.title: Controlling Mode-Locking in Liquid Light
items.abstract: Mode-locking is the process by which the phases of many cavity modes organize collectively into a stationary state. In lasers, mode-locking originates from the interplay of gain, loss, dispersion and nonlinearities, most commonly resulting in the emission of short pulses. However, pulse formation is prevented when the gain recovery is fast enough to suppress amplitude fluctuations. Mode-locking then produces an extended state of nearly constant intensity, whose dynamics is governed by the phase. Yet, a general framework for designing the phase of such extended photonic states remains lacking. Here we introduce a hydrodynamic approach to designing extended photonic states, in which the phase dynamics are understood and controlled as a flow of liquid-like light. items.title: A database of optical and thermal-radiative behaviour of materials under solar radiation
items.abstract: Solar-matter interactions are important in many scientific and engineering applications. Modeling them needs consistent optical and thermal-radiative properties over the full solar spectrum. Here we present SpaderOptics, a database for 21 materials: metals, oxides, semiconductors, polymers, ceramics, and carbon. It compiles wavelength-dependent refractive indices and extinction coefficients from the literature. Each literature source is kept separate, together with its original conditions. One physics-based calculation chain turns these data into reflectivity, transmissivity, absorptivity, and emissivity for different incidence angles, slab thicknesses, and temperatures. Combined with the Air Mass Zero (AM0) solar spectrum, the properties give absorbed, reflected, and transmitted solar flux for concentrated sunlight. items.title: Directionality of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO experiment
items.abstract: Electron-recoil directionality can help distinguish solar-neutrino interactions from backgrounds and, together with recoil-energy measurements and three-dimensional tracking, enable neutrino-energy spectroscopy. We study the reconstruction of the initial direction of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO optical time-projection chamber, focusing on the 50 L LIME prototype and its high-granularity scientific CMOS (sCMOS) readout. A dedicated algorithm identifies the interaction point from the asymmetry of the track light distribution and estimates the recoil direction from the early portion of the ionization trail, before multiple scattering erases most of the directional information. The method is characterized with a detailed Monte Carlo simulation of electron recoils and detector response. items.title: Anomalous temperature dependence of the band gap in TiNCl
items.abstract: We report an unusual nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the optical band gap in the layered nitride halide TiNCl, revealed by temperature-dependent photoluminescence (PL) and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy. The band gap, determined from the PL spectra, decreases with increasing temperature at low temperatures, reaches a minimum near 50 K, and then increases at higher temperatures. This behavior contrasts with the monotonic decrease typically observed in conventional semiconductors. The observed temperature dependence is well reproduced by a Bose-Einstein oscillator model with two characteristic phonon energies of approximately 8.9 meV and 1.2 meV. Based on temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction measurements and first-principles calculations using the experimental lattice parameters, we found that the contribution of thermal expansion is negligibly small compared with the observed...

items.title: A Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-Head Attention Model: A Surrogate for Parallel DEVS Semiconductor Fab Simulation
items.abstract: Semiconductor factories process many kinds of wafers organized into lots of various sizes and configurations. Different kinds of machines, each with its own operations, process wafers for hours to days, and the wafers undergo many incremental fabrication steps (with re-entry) and flows spanning days to weeks across connected machines. Fast and accurate predictions of throughput ($TH$) and turnaround time ($TA$) dynamics for individual machines and their combinations are essential for factory operations. To use machine learning methods for this purpose, this paper presents a Temporal Convolutional Network with Multi-head Attention (TCNA) architecture. It uses simulated datasets from a benchmark Parallel DEVS (PDEVS) semiconductor fabrication factory model. The factory processes configurable wafer lots with uniform and sinusoidal wafer arrival profiles and may undergo preventive maintenanc...

items.title: Rashba Effect and Type-III Broken-Gap Band Alignment in MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures for Tunnel Field-Effect Transistors
items.abstract: Two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures (vdWHs) based on transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising platforms for next-generation low-power electronics and spintronics. Here, we investigate the structural, electronic, and spin properties of MoTe$_2$/HfS$_2$ vdWHs using first-principles density functional theory calculations. Our results reveal an intrinsic type-III (broken-gap) band alignment, making this heterostructure highly attractive for tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) applications. In addition, inversion-symmetry breaking at the interface, combined with strong spin-orbit coupling, induces a pronounced Rashba spin splitting around the $Γ$ point, accompanied by characteristic helical spin textures. items.title: Quantum teleportation with photons from remote quantum dots emitting at telecom C-band
items.abstract: Employing quantum teleportation to increase the communication distance in quantum channels requires distinct quantum light sources, preferably operating at telecommunication wavelength. Here we utilize two semiconductor In(Ga)As quantum dots, strain engineered to emit in the telecom C-band, as sources of single- and entangled-photons, respectively. This enables a full-photonic quantum teleportation experiment, achieving a maximum teleportation fidelity of 92.7(5)%. Owing to state-of-the-art source brightness, and high time resolution, it is here possible to employ the three-photon coincidences to fully quantify the time-dependence of the process. In this way, we highlight current limitations and implement an optimization in the data-processing which leads to the maximization of achievable teleportation fidelity and coincidence rates. items.title: Exciton-polarons in monolayer semiconductors with drifting electrons
items.abstract: Recent work has demonstrated that the optical absorption of moderately doped two-dimensional semiconductors can be described in terms of exciton-polarons. In this picture, interactions between a photoexcited exciton and a Fermi sea of excess charge carriers split the exciton spectrum into a lower-energy attractive polaron branch and a higher-energy repulsive polaron branch. Due to the negligible in-plane momentum of photons, however, optical measurements probe only exciton-polarons near zero momentum, leaving their finite-momentum physics largely unexplored. Here we propose accessing this regime by measuring the absorption in the presence of an electric bias current. In effect, this displaces the electronic Fermi sea in momentum space, such that an optically active exciton-polaron at rest acquires finite momentum relative to the charge carriers. items.title: Field-Effect Magnon Transistor
items.abstract: Antiferromagnetic magnons offer a promising platform for highspeed, energy-efficient information processing. Intrinsic odd-parity spin splitting in a cycloidal magnetic order offers a route to nonvanishing magnon transport in compensated magnets. Here, we propose a magnonic field-effect device (akin to a transistor) based on a ferroelectric antiferromagnet BiFeO3 in which a gate electric field reconfigures domain boundaries to amplify/modulate magnon transport. These boundaries switch the nonlocal inverse-spin-Hall response between low- and high-signal states, with a pronounced dependence on the direction of magnon propagation. Source-drain reversal, magnetic-field measurements, symmetry analysis, and first-principles calculations reveal nonreciprocal magnon transport associated with the reversal of spin angular momentum across the domain boundaries. In particular, lane-level defects, limited spares, and strict structural compatibility requirements impede the efficient assembly of functional systems from defective but repairable chiplets. We present DT-MATCH, a defect- and topology-aware chiplet matching framework that maximizes the number of functional SoCs under realistic assembly constraints. Here we introduce a self-emissive tactile imaging strategy based on alternating-current electroluminescence (ACEL) devices, in which a compressible porous dielectric encodes contact pressure into spatial emission patterns without external illumination or discrete sensing pixels. items.title: Power Scaling Across Link Utilization with GPAM-4 Signaling and Event-Driven Reception
items.abstract: This work highlights the potential of combining event-based signaling with event-driven reception to achieve receiver power scaling across link utilization, without requiring wake-up, locking, or data-rate reconfiguration. The approach is demonstrated using the proposed four-level Gaussian pulse-amplitude modulation (GPAM-4) scheme and a corresponding event-driven receiver. By employing a resettable ring voltage-controlled oscillator (RRVCO) as its front end, the receiver achieves inherently event-driven symbol measurement, initiated directly by each received pulse. Symbols are decoded directly from the final RRVCO phase state, eliminating a counter-based back end. items.abstract: The ability to optically control the valley degree of freedom in two-dimensional semiconductors is critical for scalable valleytronics. While magnetic proximity effects can lift valley degeneracy, static interfaces lack the dynamic control needed for devices. items.title: Pressure and Magnetic Field Control of Topology in Antiferromagnetic Bilayers
items.abstract: Controlling band topology in magnetic semiconductors requires strategies that couple electronic structure to experimentally accessible degrees of freedom. Here we propose a cooperative approach based on pressure and magnetic reorientation in A-type antiferromagnetic bilayers. Antiparallel layer magnetizations suppress hybridization between exchange-polarized band-edge states, limiting their response to interlayer compression. A magnetic field that aligns the layer moments removes this spin mismatch, enabling pressure-enhanced hybridization to drive a band inversion. The magnetization direction then controls the symmetries of the inverted bands and whether spin--orbit coupling produces a Chern-insulating gap or symmetry-protected nodal crossings. items.title: EventSpikeSeg: Memory-Aware Mixed-Signal Architecture for Event-Camera Spiking Segmentation
items.abstract: Event-camera segmentation requires persistent neural state despite sparse input events, making memory organization a central constraint on embedded implementation. We present EventSpikeSeg, a mixed-signal architecture combining resident capacitor memory with shared analog processing in GF180MCU 180-nm CMOS. Its 25-population spiking encoder-decoder has 143,824 synaptic weights but requires 30,976,000 membrane states at 440 x 640 resolution. The mapping specifies chronological 5-ms model updates, digital event/address services and 64-state capacitor banks. Characterization covers 22 module families and 74 operating points, distinguishing transistor simulations from digital-library estimates. items.abstract: Interfacial coupling in van der Waals two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offers an effective route to tailor the electronic, optical, and magnetic properties of materials. Versatile control and precise engineering of such interlayer interactions can be further achieved through external parameters, like electric field, magnetic field, optical excitation, as well as layer stacking geometries. We identified a type-II band alignment between these two layers and the magnetic proximity effects from CrSBr, manifested by an enhanced Zeeman valley splitting in the WS2 layer. items.title: Mapping the Phase Space of Cubic Chiral Semiconductors: High-Throughput Search,Stability, and Prototype Families
items.abstract: Chiral crystals show unique electronic, magnetic, and optical characteristics that make them attractive for topological and spintronic applications. Nevertheless, the limited set of identified chiral semiconductors, especially those with cubic symmetry, has so far constrained their technological application. In this work, we perform a high-throughput computational search for semiconducting chiral compounds in the cubic space group $P4_332$ (No. 212). By integrating machine-learning techniques with density functional theory, we obtain 24\,227 cubic chiral structures containing up to five elements, and identify 368 thermodynamically stable semiconductors on the convex hull and 3\,048 within 50~meV/atom. items.title: Ultrafast Imaging Reveals Energy Transport Anisotropy Grows from Bulk to Monolayer Black Phosphorus
items.abstract: Black phosphorus is an emerging low-dimensional semiconductor whose tunable band gap, high carrier mobility, and anisotropic transport make it attractive for directional energy transport in electronics and thermoelectrics. Using ultrafast stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy (stroboSCAT), we image spatiotemporal evolution of energy carriers with picosecond resolution, simultaneously resolving heat and charge transport in bulk black phosphorus and exciton transport in the monolayer. The in-plane armchair:zigzag anisotropy increases from 5.3:1 in the bulk to 6.7:1 in the monolayer, driven by enhanced armchair exciton diffusivity (45.5 cm$^2$/s) relative to bulk armchair charge carriers (16.5 cm$^2$/s). items.title: Contrastive local learning in large nonlinear analog circuits
items.abstract: Machine learning in physical hardware promises to reduce training cost by colocating computation, memory and adaptation within device physics. Contrastive local learning networks (CLLNs) offer a compelling route: an electrical circuit relaxes to equilibrium in free and weakly clamped states, and each adaptive element updates from local voltage contrasts rather than backpropagated error signals. Yet whether nonlinear transistor implementations can scale beyond proof-of-concept circuits, and what design principles control that scaling, have remained unknown. Here we show that nonlinear analog circuits trained by contrastive local rules can learn larger machine-learning tasks and remain robust under hardware nonidealities. Using device-level circuit simulations, we systematically explore initialization, operating regime, loss-dependent clamping and training parameters, and scale CLLNs beyon...

items.title: Composition Driven Band Alignment Evolution in Grafted Si/GeSn Heterostructures
items.abstract: Understanding and controlling band alignment in lattice-mismatched group-IV semiconductor-based heterostructures is fundamental to rational band-structure engineering, as it governs the electronic structure and carrier transport in heterointegrated semiconductor systems. Despite growing interest in Si/GeSn heterostructures, the composition-dependent band alignment has not been experimentally established. Here, we experimentally establish the evolution of band alignment in semiconductor-grafted Si/GeSn heterostructures with contents ranging from 8.8% to 12.4% using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and Kraut's core-level method. The valence-band offset increases systematically from ~0.29 to ~0.57 eV with increasing Sn composition, whereas the corresponding effective conduction-band offset decreases from ~0.30 to ~0.12 eV. The observed band-alignment evolution is attributed to an upward shi...

items.title: AnalogLayoutWorld: An Open Benchmark for Agentic Analog Layout Design
items.abstract: Coding agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in software development, yet their ability to tackle long-horizon engineering tasks governed by physical constraints remains less understood. We study this question through analog circuit layout, which demands domain knowledge, geometric reasoning, and iterative interaction with design and verification tools. We introduce \textbf{AnalogLayoutWorld}, an open-source agent benchmark with 40 expert-reviewed tasks for end-to-end layout generation from fixed transistor-level netlists. It combines an integrated design environment with independent physical and post-layout electrical verification, as well as objective layout quality metrics co-designed with analog layout experts. items.title: Gatemon qubits based on in-situ ternary InAsSb/Al nanowire Josephson junctions
items.abstract: Ternary InAsSb/Al nanowires combine compositionally engineerable semiconductor properties with epitaxial proximity superconductivity, making them attractive for hybrid quantum circuits and mesoscopic superconductivity. Here, we realize gatemon qubits based on shadow-defined in-situ InAsSb/Al Josephson junctions in a single growth process. Gate-dependent microwave spectroscopy demonstrates electrostatic tuning of the qubit transition over several gigahertz. Rabi oscillations and Ramsey interference show coherent qubit control, with representative values T1 = 0.79 us and T2* = 0.91 us. Across five gatemons distributed over three chips, the measured relaxation times range from approximately 0.2 us to 1 us and decrease with increasing qubit frequency. items.abstract: MALTA2 is a monolithic active pixel sensor, developed in the 180 nm CMOS imaging technology for radiation-hard applications in high-rate environments. The charge collection of a sensor on epitaxial silicon is studied with the Edge Transient Current Technique (Edge-TCT), using a digital readout, where the charge is reconstructed solely from binary hit data. In previous works, only specially designed analog output pixels at the matrix periphery were investigated. In contrast, the digital readout gives access to the full edge of the pixel matrix. Laser scans across neighboring pixels enable a two-dimensional parameterization of the charge collection. items.title: Bright and Uniform Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic Arrays for Scalable Nanoscale Quantum Sensing
items.abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) spin defects are emerging as powerful platforms for nanoscale quantum sensing due to their near-surface stability, near-infrared emission, and CMOS compatibility. However, poor photon collection efficiency and the reliance on randomly distributed defects hinder the realization of practical, large-scale devices. Here, we demonstrate scalable, ultra-bright, and highly uniform SiC quantum nanophotonic arrays. By combining a self-aligned fabrication process with localized oxygen ion implantation, we deterministically position PL5 and PL6 centers at the exact center of 4H-SiC nanopillars. This architecture yields record-high photon count rates of $\sim$1 Mcps (PL5) and $\sim$2 Mcps (PL6), establishing a new benchmark for SiC color centers while maintaining near-identical brightness across the array. items.abstract: Semiconductor InSb nanowires are a major material candidate for topological quantum computation. The nanowires in current devices were mostly grown using metal organic chemical vapor deposition, incompatible with in situ growth of superconductor, a crucial requirement for low-disorder devices. Growth of InSb nanowires using molecular-beam epitaxy (MBE) can address this issue. So far, studies on MBE-grown InSb remain limited due to an extremely narrow parameter window for the growth and reproducibility. Moreover, the use of foreign catalysts can introduce deep-level impurities. Here, we report a self-catalyzed MBE growth of InSb nanowires without those foreign catalysts. items.abstract: Chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) is a critical semiconductor manufacturing process where material removal rate (MRR) is a key metric for process monitoring and advanced process control (APC). Virtual metrology enables MRR estimation from process time series signals, supporting run-to-run(R2R) control and process optimization while reducing reliance on physical metrology. Existing approaches typically rely on simplified linear assumptions or require handcrafted feature engineering. In this paper, we propose Global Regression Pretraining(GREP), a self-supervised, attention-based framework for CMP MRR prediction. GREP learns temporal representations from unlabeled sensor signals through global proxy-target regression, followed by supervised fine-tuning for MRR estimation. items.abstract: T centres in silicon combine an optical transition in the telecom O-band with a long-lived electron and nuclear spin in a photonics- and CMOS-compatible host. However, weak emission of photons in the zero-phonon line (ZPL) makes measurements slow. Cavities can increase the ZPL photon emission, but high-Q cavities require individual tuning to the T centre wavelength, hindering statistical understanding of T centre properties. The combination of high accuracy and moderate quality factors removes the need for individual tuning. items.title: Ground-state phase diagram of the spin-1/2 Heisenberg zigzag ladder with anisotropic $Γ$ term revisited
items.abstract: We study the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet with an anisotropic $Γ$ term on a zigzag ladder, which can be exactly mapped to the spin-1/2 XYZ zigzag ladder by a spin rotation. This model has recently attracted considerable interest as an effective model for the quasi-one-dimensional magnetic semiconductor YbCuS$_2$. For the model, the ground-state phase diagram was previously proposed by Saito and Hotta [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 166701 (2024); Phys. Rev. B 110, 024409 (2024)]. We systematically reexamine the phase diagram through complementary numerical and analytical approaches, including exact diagonalization, the density-matrix renormalization group method, and low-energy effective theories. We thereby demonstrate that when the anisotropic $Γ$ term is present, the model exhibits the Néel, dimer, ferromagnetic, and double-Néel phases, all of which have a finite excitation gap. The gap...

items.title: Neutronic Field-Effect Transistor
items.abstract: Field-effect electronic devices are in widespread use in communication, computing, data storage, and sensing applications. We demonstrate a neutronic field-effect transistor (NFET) that is analogous to the Datta-Das electron spin transistor and atomtronic devices. The NFET is based on a perfect-crystal Mach-Zehnder neutron interferometer with phase shifts applied to the spin and path degrees of freedom.

items.title: Spin-valve effect through electrostatic coupling
items.abstract: We propose a spin-valve effect in which an insulating magnetic van der Waals multilayer controls the conductance of an adjacent non-magnetic conductor by electrostatic coupling, without transport-electrons entering the magnetic layers. The coupling is induced by the variations of the electronic structure when the relative orientation of the magnetization of adjacent monolayers changes from parallel to antiparallel, modifying both the dielectric constant and band alignment. We consider two types of coupling and device concepts: charge transfer to a graphene monolayer and capacitive coupling in a single-electron transistor. We use density functional calculations to assess the magnitude of the effect in various materials, including CrI$_3$, CrBr$_3$, CrCl$_3$ and NiBr$_2$. items.title: Gate-tunable supercurrent switching in a three-terminal quantum dot transistor
items.abstract: We propose and analyze a three-terminal superconducting transistor switch in which a gate-defined quantum dot region interrupts a flux-controlled loop. The output supercurrent is switched off completely when the two loop arms couple to the dot with equal tunneling strengths and half a flux quantum threads the loop. The device then operates as a symmetric SQUID at half flux. The condition follows from a single geometric factor $χ$, which reduces the three-terminal problem to an equivalent two-terminal Anderson impurity model and makes the switching mechanism independent of the Coulomb interaction, the dot level position, the total hybridization and temperature. These enter only through a prefactor and thus decide how tolerant the device is to imperfect barrier tuning. items.title: Rapid Heat Removal from Chip Cores: Near-Junction Active Cooling of Power Transistors via Electron Entropy Transport and Spatial Decoupling
items.abstract: Chip performance is limited by a shared bottleneck: the core produces heat faster than it can be moved out. We study the hardest case, RF power GaN HEMTs, whose hotspots exceed 5 kW/cm^2, and propose a horizontal near-junction active cooling topology built on electron entropy transport. Classical on-chip thermoelectric cooling faces a contest: Peltier absorption grows linearly with current, Joule heating with its square. In a vertical pillar, its own conduction resistance locks about half the Joule heat back toward the cold end, capping net cooling. From the Onsager framework we show the origin of this asymmetry: Peltier absorption localizes at the interface where the Seebeck coefficient jumps, whereas Joule heating fills the volume. items.title: Orbital texture of valence band and interband transitions of the type-II multiferroic van der Waals NiI$_2$
items.abstract: NiI$_2$ is a van der Waals semiconductor characterized by complex electronic and magnetic phases, holding promise towards functional applications. For this purpose, a detailed understanding of its band structure and its excitations is essential to elucidate the electronic and transport properties. We present a comprehensive description of the band structure and of the lowest valence-to-conduction band transition in bulk NiI$_2$, by means of time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy supported by first-principles calculations. We describe the orbital character of Ni and I manifolds, and identify the main momentum-resolved features of the valence band and the shallow minima of the conduction band. With this study, we provide a foundational understanding of the electronic structure of NiI$_2$ and its single-particle interband electronic excitation, a benchmark for theoretical model...

items.title: A Per-Step Load-Balancing Engine for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving
items.abstract: In expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts serving, a layer finishes only when the most loaded GPU of its group does. Token routing shifts at every decode step and concentrates on a few experts, so most of the group's reserved GPU time waits on stragglers. Recovering that time means re-deciding, at every layer of every decode step, how each replicated expert's tokens divide between its copies. The exact linear-program solvers that make this decision optimally take longer than many of the layers they serve, and their working set outgrows GPU shared memory at deployment scale. We introduce Relief, a bidirectional pairwise relaxation that makes the linear program unnecessary, coming within a fraction of a point of the per-step optimum in a few passes of integer halving over the token counts. items.title: ICLayout-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Custom Circuit Layout Design
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are being explored for circuit design, but their ability to produce high-quality custom layouts has not been extensively evaluated. ICLayout-Bench is a benchmark in which agents use electronic design automation (EDA) tools to construct and optimize GDSII layouts from transistor-level circuit netlists. These layouts are evaluated using physical verification, parasitic extraction, and post-layout simulation. Layouts that pass the physical and functional checks are scored on electrical performance and area. The benchmark includes 165 tasks across 13 process design kits (PDKs), covering technology nodes from 3 nm to 180 nm. The tasks span analog, mixed-signal, and digital circuits in open-source and commercial EDA flows. The experiments evaluate 22 configurations spanning seven models on 21 public and 19 private tasks. items.title: $>3\text{ W/mm}$ Output Power $\mathrm{Al}_{0.61}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.39}\mathrm{N}$ Channel HEMT with $24.4\%$ Associated PAE at $10\text{ GHz}$
items.abstract: In this work, an ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) was fabricated using an $\mathrm{Al}_{0.76}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.24}\mathrm{N}$ barrier and an $\mathrm{Al}_{0.61}\mathrm{Ga}_{0.39}\mathrm{N}$ channel with thick $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ passivation. The device demonstrated low current collapse at $40\text{ V}$ drain bias. At $10\text{ GHz}$, the device exhibited an output power of $3.07\text{ W/mm}$ with an associated power-added efficiency (PAE) of $24.4\%$. A peak PAE of $33.9\%$ was achieved at an associated output power of $2.14\text{ W/mm}$. This excellent large-signal performance highlights the strong potential of UWBG $\mathrm{AlGaN}$ channel devices for X-band applications.

items.abstract: A new approach to discretise and solve Richards equation based on the finite element method (FEM) is presented. items.abstract: Time-resolved infrared (TR-IR) spectroscopy reveals molecular structural changes and charge-carrier dynamics on their intrinsic timescales, in photosynthesis, catalysis and optoelectronic materials, but requires complex sources of ultrashort infrared pulses, cryogenically cooled detectors to overcome thermal background, and intense probes that can perturb the sample. items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VI. Surface diffusion on a nonmetal-terminated surface
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate surface diffusion of adsorbates on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the adsorption processes on Ga-terminated surfaces of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. The considered adsorbates are nonmetal species, i.e., nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, and antimony on wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e., GaN(0001) surfaces, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e., GaP(111), gallium arsenide, GaAs(111), and gallium antimonide, GaSb (111) surfaces. The structural and electronic properties of the stoichiometric polar surfaces of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors (GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb), i.e. metal- and nonmetal-terminated were determined. items.title: 10 kV $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Sub-Bandgap Triggered Impurity Photoconductive Semiconductor Switches (i-PCSSs): Lessons for Optimal Design
items.abstract: $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ photoconductive semiconductor switches (PCSSs) are attractive for high-voltage operation, but above-bandgap triggering requires deep-ultraviolet excitation. Here, we investigate a 650-um-thick, 0.01% Fe-doped $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ impurity PCSS with a 5-mm lateral gap under continuous-wave (CW) 808-nm sub-bandgap excitation at biases up to 10 kV ( 20 kV cm^-1). The device exhibited clear sub-bandgap photoconductive switching. As the optical power density increased from 0.64 to 3.18 W cm^-2, the ON-state current increased progressively while the ON-state resistance decreased, consistent with enhanced defect-assisted photocarrier generation. items.title: HAWK: Heterogeneity-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Efficient GPU-NPU Phase-Disaggregated LLM Inference
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference exhibits distinct computational characteristics across its two phases: prefill is compute-intensive, whereas decode is more memory-bound. As a result, AI accelerators achieve varying levels of efficiency across the two phases. GPUs are well suited to prefill, but are often underutilized during decode. By contrast, NPUs can utilize their compute resources more effectively during decode. Motivated by this observation, we explore a heterogeneous architecture that integrates GPUs and NPUs, mapping prefill to GPUs and decode to NPUs to achieve high performance and efficiency. However, realizing such heterogeneous integration is challenging because LLM phase disaggregation requires KV cache transfer from prefill to decode (that is, from GPUs to NPUs), which is complicated by differences in inter-device communication mechanisms and KV cache tensor layouts. items.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
items.abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $μ$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

items.title: Adjoint-State Identifiability of Piezo-Tunable Valley Splitting in 2D Magnetic Heterostructures
items.abstract: Mechanical strain has been proposed to dynamically tune proximity-induced valley splitting in 2D magnetic heterostructures for solid-state information processing. While first-principles studies routinely predict strain-modulated valley splittings at the atomic scale, they rarely address whether the coupling parameter can be extracted from a macroscopic transport measurement against realistic device noise. This paper develops a classical, partial differential equation-constrained multiscale inverse framework to quantify the device-level identifiability of the exchange-strain coupling from a transverse Hall voltage in a molybdenum disulfide and chromium tribromide heterostructure. Structural relaxation confirms a chiral $C_3$ point-group symmetry of the Hollow-stacked structure, and Neumann's principle reduces the coupling tensor to a single scalar $η$. Dispersion-corrected density functio...

items.title: SyclKittens: A Tile Programming Model for Programmers and Coding Agents on Intel GPUs
items.abstract: New AI accelerators arrive before the kernels that make them fast, because peak kernel performance requires architecture-specific expertise in operand pipelines and data-movement techniques. Coding agents can now write, compile, and tune kernels on their own, so they could greatly accelerate kernel development and optimization. What agents produce depends on the interfaces they are given. These interfaces may expose a machine's raw capabilities or encode the known-good methods for exploiting its hardware features efficiently. We test the performance impact of these two interfaces on Intel GPUs through controlled experiments with five coding models on three kernels. With raw SYCL and execution feedback, Opus 4.8, the strongest of the three models tested with Claude Code, writes a single-GPU GEMM kernel reaching only 57.5% of Intel's tuned oneDNN library. We present SyclKittens, a hardware...

items.title: Theoretical study of nitrogen-vacancy spin coherence enhanced by vacancy aggregation in diamond using cluster-correlation expansion
items.abstract: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for the decoherence of negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) centres in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations in which the spins outside each cluster keep exchanging spin projections in pairs reproduce the measured Hahn-echo coherence time of NV$^-$ centres in a substitutional-nitrogen bath to within 12%, inside the statistical uncertainty. Driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters, the same calculation inverts the attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hah...

items.title: Prescreening Point Defects in Semiconductors With Machine Learning
items.abstract: High-throughput calculations using density-functional theory (DFT) are commonly used to explore point defects for applications in power electronics and quantum technologies. There is currently a major shift away from these traditional simulation techniques towards machine learning (ML) methods. We explore a class of physics-guided ML models for predicting defect formation energies and zero-phonon lines (ZPL) to identify point defects for quantum applications. The models are specifically targeted for use in a prescreening step for accelerated high-throughput workflows, and are therefore designed to avoid the costly relaxation step typically present with ML interatomic potentials (MLIPs). We compare performance for single and double point defect systems in 4H-SiC with ridge, kernel ridge, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models using three different descriptors representing the defect syste...

items.title: Density-gradient effect in high-harmonic generation in gases
items.abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) in gaseous targets is the most widespread method to produce coherent extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) pulses with sub-femtosecond duration. However, this process has intrinsically low efficiency, and substantial research and development is devoted worldwide to increase the achievable photon flux through this highly nonlinear light--matter interaction process. In this work, we show the strong interplay of phase matching and absorption in gas-pressure gradients, substantially affecting macroscopic HHG efficiency. Through detailed experimental analysis and supporting numerical studies, we highlight their significance, particularly at the boundaries of the interaction volume. The concluded results have implications in the massively expanding application possibilities of HHG sources requiring high photon flux, for example in the semiconductor industry, in nanoscale ima...

items.title: Optical Voltage Profiling of 2D Semiconductors via Proximal Exciton Sensing
items.abstract: High contact resistances in atomically thin semiconductors often mask intrinsic electrical transport properties, particularly at low carrier densities where exotic correlated states emerge. We introduce optical voltage profiling, a noninvasive wide-field technique that replaces local voltage probes with a proximal monolayer MoSe$_2$ exciton sensor. Isolated by thin hexagonal boron nitride, this sensor converts the target's local voltage into spatially resolved modulations of exciton reflectance. Through pixel-wise in situ calibration, these signals yield quantitative two-dimensional voltage maps of an actively biased semiconductor device. Using this method, we demonstrate the carrier-density-driven metal-insulator transition in bilayer MoSe$_2$ and obtain channel resistances of a few k$Ω$ despite M$Ω$-scale two-terminal resistances in the metallic region. The optically derived resistance...

items.title: Emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi Surfaces in hybrid Al/InAs heterostructures
items.abstract: We investigate the microwave electrodynamics of a proximitized two-dimensional electron gas in hybrid superconductor/semiconductor heterostructures. Using lumped-element resonators with inductor wires oriented relative to an in-plane magnetic field, we directly probe the superfluid stiffness via the kinetic inductance. As the field increases, the resonance frequency exhibits a non-monotonic and strongly anisotropic evolution that cannot be explained by orbital pair breaking alone. We show that this behavior is consistent with the emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces, which selectively suppress the supercurrent response depending on the direction of the magnetic field. Microscopic calculations of the stiffness tensor capture the observed anisotropy driven by the interplay of Zeeman and orbital Fulde-Ferrell effects. items.title: Bright and Dark Excitons in CrSBr: Local Ligand-Field Character and Band-Coherent Optical Selection Rules
items.abstract: Magnetic van der Waals semiconductors such as CrSBr host an intricate exciton landscape. Quasiparticle self-consistent GW theory with electron-hole ladder vertex corrections (QSGWc) has established the gap and the character of the bright XA (1.34 eV) and XB (1.8 eV) excitons. Why these bright excitons coexist, within a few tens of meV, with companions orders of magnitude darker has remained unexplained. Here we show that brightness is fixed by a symmetry of the structure: a mirror-glide exchanges the two Cr atoms of each layer, every exciton has a definite parity under it, and bright and dark partners are its even and odd members. The even sector carries the b-axis dipole; the odd sector is suppressed by about three orders of magnitude. The dark partners of XA and XB occupy the same region of k-space as the bright states, and dark states such as the one at 1.50 eV are dipole-forbidden by...

items.title: Multi-stage Quantum Amplifier Readout Chain
items.abstract: Multi-stage cryogenic readout chains with a wide bandwidth and added noise within a few quanta of the quantum limit are frequently constructed using traveling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPAs) as the first stage, and a semiconductor amplifier as the second stage. Unfortunately, for highly-scaled superconducting detector arrays, or quantum information systems, and space-based observatories, the power dissipation of the semiconductor amplifier becomes problematic from the perspective of available cryogenic cooling power near 3 K. Here we demonstrate a readout chain based on a two-stage kinetic inductance TWPA (KTWPA). This quantum-amplifier-based-readout-chain (QARC) provides sufficient gain that a cryogenic semiconductor follow-on amplifier can be eliminated without degradation of the system noise. Due to the ultra-low dissipation of KTWPAs and their higher output-power-to-total-power ra...

items.title: Photon-conserving Raman soliton attractors in focusing and defocusing Kerr media
items.abstract: The sign of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient has long been regarded as irrelevant to the direction of the Raman-induced soliton self-frequency shift. Yet the standard generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) predicts a frequency shift that depends on the sign of the nonlinearity, which leads to an unphysical blue shift in the defocusing case. We resolve this inconsistency by deriving the time-domain form of the photon-conserving GNLSE (pcGNLSE) from its established frequency-domain counterpart. The derivation reveals that photon-number conservation imposes two sign modifications relative to the standard GNLSE: the Raman-shift coefficient acquires the absolute value of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient in place of its signed counterpart, and the self-steepening-Raman dissipation term likewise carries an absolute-value prefactor rather than a signed one. items.title: Transmon Phase Gates Controlled by Superconducting Soliton DAC
items.abstract: We introduce a superconducting digital-to-analog converter (DAC) that filters control noise, provides native multiplexing, performs quantum gates in nanoseconds, and can be controlled by CMOS. This is achieved by transducing a trapezoidal drive pulse into a superconducting soliton, which is then held in the DAC load loop, applying flux to a mutually-coupled superconducting qubit or gate coupler. The analog flux output by the DAC can be easily controlled by varying the soliton hold time, or with a DC-biased tunable DAC-qubit coupler, allowing the DAC to perform a fixed-time, high-fidelity gate that's robust to fabrication variance or flux offsets in the quantum circuit. Our initial demonstration shows that the DAC can successfully perform 5.6 ns S-gates on transmons. We measure the DAC-induced quantum state excitation probability per gate to be 0.05%, and find that the DAC-induced relaxat...

items.title: Carruthers Data Processing Pipeline: Instrument Effect Correction
items.abstract: The Carruthers Geocorona Observatory -- launched in September 2025 -- is NASA's first mission devoted to investigating the fundamental nature of Earth's exosphere from its distant vantage in halo orbit around the Earth-Sun L1 Lagrange point. Its primary payload, the GeoCoronal Imager, consists of two coaligned photometric imagers that measure ultraviolet Lyman-alpha emission radiance from exospheric hydrogen simultaneously at wide- and narrow- fields of view. The imagers use MicroChannel Plate intensified Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor detectors, which are known to add various artifacts to the final image telemetered from the spacecraft, hereby known as instrument effects. This paper details the algorithms used to retrieve and remove instrument effects from raw telemetry on-orbit, including detector voltage bias, thermal dark current, particle radiation, flat-field, and distorti...

items.title: Designing Strong and Broadband Nonreciprocal Thermal Radiation in Magnetic Topological Materials
items.abstract: Breaking reciprocity in thermal radiation opens opportunities for energy harvesting, sensing, and thermal management. Traditional nonreciprocal radiative semiconductor devices need external magnetic field. In this work, we predict a series of magnetic topological materials for magnetic-field-free nonreciprocal thermal radiation in the infrared regime, by combining first-principles calculations with Maxwell electrodynamics. We find strong and broadband nonreciprocity in magnetic Weyl semimetals (e.g., Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$), outperforming the conventional semiconductor such as InAs. Furthermore, we propose universal material design recipes: strong nonreciprocity requires a large anomalous Hall response relative to the optical loss, whereas the broadband response favors large optical loss and small dielectric dispersion.
